courses.name: General Physics II
weekTopics: Magnetism and magnetic field lines: every magnet has a north and a south pole, like poles repel and unlike attract, the field is mapped with iron filings or a compass, it is stronger where the lines are denser, and because there are no magnetic monopoles every line of B is a closed loop running N to S outside the magnet and S to N inside it

A magnetic dipole and its two models: a current loop and a pair of separated poles give the same field far from the source but different predictions inside the source region, the current-loop model being the physically correct one
Magnetic dipole moment mu = IA for one turn and mu = NIA for N turns, a vector along the normal to the loop with its sense given by the right-hand rule, measured in A*m^2 (equivalently J/T)

Torque on a dipole in a uniform field, torque = mu x B with magnitude mu*B*sin(theta) where theta is the angle between mu and B, maximum when the plane of the loop contains B and zero when mu lies along B; the net force in a uniform field is zero, so the dipole turns but does not translate
Potential energy of a dipole, U = -mu.B = -mu*B*cos(theta), minimum -mu*B at alignment (stable) and maximum +mu*B when anti-aligned (unstable), so the work to flip a dipole end for end is 2*mu*B

Magnetic dipole moment of an electron, M = g(-eL/2m), where the minus sign records that the moment is antiparallel to the angular momentum because the charge is negative and g is the g-factor (about 1 for orbital motion and about 2 for spin), giving the Bohr magneton eh-bar/2m = 9.27e-24 J/T

Fields produced by currents: B = mu_0*I/(2*pi*r) in closed circles around a long straight wire, B = mu_0*N*I/(2R) at the centre of a flat coil, and B = mu*n*I inside a long solenoid where n = N/L is turns per unit length and the core permeability multiplies the result
Applications of magnetic dipoles: NMR tomography and MRI, electric motors, credit-card magnetic strips, and the Earth as a dipole whose field reverses roughly every 200 thousand years

courses.name: Elementary Mathematics II (Calculus)
weekTopics: Integration has no algorithm the way differentiation does, so every technique this week is a way of converting an integral you cannot do into a standard form you can, and the working stops only when a table entry is reached - checked, as always, by differentiating the answer back

The standard integrals extended beyond Week 7 to the forms the techniques aim at: (integral of f'(x)/f(x) dx) = ln|f(x)|, (integral of dx/(a^2 + x^2)) = (1/a) arctan(x/a), (integral of dx/sqrt(a^2 - x^2)) = arcsin(x/a), (integral of dx/(x^2 - a^2)) = (1/2a) ln|(x - a)/(x + a)|, and (integral of tan x dx) = ln|sec x|

Integration by substitution as the reverse of the chain rule: u = g(x) with du = g'(x) dx works only when g'(x) is present in the integrand up to a constant multiple, a numerical factor may be moved across the integral sign to fix du but a function of x never may, a leftover x is removed by solving u = g(x) back for x, and a definite integral must either have its limits converted to u-values or be returned to x first

Integration by parts as the reverse of the product rule: integrating d(uv) = u dv + v du gives (integral of u dv) = uv - (integral of v du), which trades one integral for another rather than evaluating it, so u is chosen by LIATE - logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, algebraic, trigonometric, exponential - and dv must be something that can actually be integrated

The three standard uses of parts: repeated application, once per power of x, for integrands like x^2 sin x; the dv = dx trick that makes (integral of ln x dx) = x ln x - x possible at all; and the cycling integrals (integral of e^x sin x dx) and (integral of e^x cos x dx), where the original integral I reappears and the answer comes from solving 2I = ... algebraically

Trigonometric substitution for a square root of a quadratic: x = a sin(theta) for sqrt(a^2 - x^2) using 1 - sin^2 = cos^2, x = a tan(theta) for sqrt(a^2 + x^2) using 1 + tan^2 = sec^2, and x = a sec(theta) for sqrt(x^2 - a^2) using sec^2 - 1 = tan^2, with the theta-range chosen so no modulus is needed and with the return to x made through the right-angled triangle rather than left in theta

Partial fractions for rational integrands: long-divide first whenever the numerator's degree is not strictly less than the denominator's, then give each distinct linear factor a constant numerator, each repeated linear factor (x - a)^k one term for every power from 1 to k, and each irreducible quadratic a linear numerator Ax + B which then splits into an f'/f logarithm and an arctan

Choosing the technique from the shape of the integrand rather than its difficulty: a composite with its inner derivative present is a substitution, a numerator that is the derivative of the denominator is a bare logarithm, a product of two unrelated types is parts, a root over a quadratic is a trigonometric substitution, and a ratio of polynomials is division followed by partial fractions

courses.name: Introduction to Problem Solving
weekTopics: Abstraction is defined as the process of hiding the internal details of an application from the outer world, illustrated by the car ignition analogy in which the driver twists the key without concerning themselves with what happens in the engine in between

The two named types of abstraction: data abstraction, in which the data of an object is not directly exposed to other programmes and no other programme can alter that data without obtaining the necessary permissions; and functional abstraction, in which the implementation of an object's methods is not exposed and a caller is given only the method's name, the format of the input and the format of the output

The two mechanisms for implementing abstraction - access specifiers, where public and private are applied to the properties and functions of an object and restrict the access of other programmes to only some of them, and header files, which let you use a library's functions without any knowledge of how each is implemented - and the four stated benefits: applications are more secure because the implementation is not exposed, code readability and reusability are enhanced, the implementation of a method can be changed without breaking other parts of the code, and duplication of code is prevented

Why complex projects are decomposed: a large project is impossible or time-wasting for one person, so it is broken into functions that different people can work on at the same time; functions let a project scale up because a project that becomes complex only needs more functions added and the system remains stable, and they avoid duplicating code because a function is implemented once however many times it is used

A function is a group of statements that perform a task, with the division of code among functions left to the programmer but made logically so that each function performs a specific task; a function declaration tells the compiler about the name, return type and parameters, while a function definition provides the actual body and consists of a function header plus a function body

The four parts of a function definition: the return type, which is the data type of the value returned and can also be void; the function name; the parameters, each a placeholder that receives a value when the function is invoked, with a function permitted to have none; and the function body, the collection of statements defining what the function does - together with parameters versus arguments, return versus print, and local versus global scope

Modules are functions at a much larger scale because they can contain various functions and classes, and are brought into use by importing: 'import special_functions' makes the module available, while 'from special_functions import max' explicitly specifies one function so that only that function may be used - the same job C does with header files and #include

Writing and reading simple C: all C programmes have main() as the entry-point function, comments run from /* to */, braces describe the start and end of a function block, printf() is a standard library function that prints a character string to standard output, and the escape sequences \' \" \\ \0 \a \b \f \n \r \t \v carry the meanings single quote, double quote, backslash, null, bell, backspace, form feed, newline, carriage return, horizontal tab and vertical tab

courses.name: General Physics Practical II
weekTopics: Aim of the experiment: to verify Boyle's law, which states that at constant temperature the pressure of a definite (fixed) quantity of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to its volume, written PV = constant, P proportional to 1/V, or P1*V1 = P2*V2

Pressure defined and its units: P = F/A, the SI unit being the pascal (1 Pa = 1 N/m^2), with the conversions 1 atm = 76 cmHg = 760 mmHg = 1.013 x 10^5 Pa and 1 ml = 1 cm^3 = 1 x 10^-6 m^3 needed throughout the analysis

Place of Boyle's law in the theory of gases: published by Robert Boyle in 1662 and discovered independently by Edme Mariotte in 1679 (the Boyle-Mariotte law), and one of the empirical laws - with Charles's, Avogadro's and Gay-Lussac's laws - that combine into the ideal gas law underpinning the kinetic theory of gases

Apparatus and the J-tube: a J-tube with one closed end and one open end, a thermometer, a pressure sensor, a gas sample and the Praxilabs virtual Boyle's Law laboratory; mercury poured into the open end traps a fixed column of air in the closed limb, and when the mercury stands at the same level in both limbs (h = 0) the trapped air is at atmospheric pressure

Pressure and volume of the trapped gas: raising the open limb so that the mercury levels differ by a vertical height h raises the pressure by rho*g*h, giving P_f = P_a + rho*g*h with rho = 13600 kg/m^3 and g = 9.8 m/s^2, while the volume follows from the length of the trapped air column, V_f = l*A, the bore being uniform with A = 1 cm^2 so that V_f is numerically equal to l

Procedure in order: begin with the mercury level in both limbs (h = 0) and record the initial volume and temperature, raise the open limb to h = 50 mm and note that the air column has shortened, click Record to log the volume, repeat in 50 mm steps through h = 100, 150, 200 and 250 mm recording the volume at each height, then download the Excel data sheet and compute P_f and 1/V_f for every row

The graph and what it means: P against V at constant temperature is a rectangular hyperbola (an isotherm) that approaches but never meets either axis and proves nothing by eye, whereas P against 1/V (or the deck's 1/V against P) is a straight line through the origin - that line is the verification; the gradient of P against 1/V equals the constant PV (2.026 J for the sample gas, since P0*V0 = 1.013 x 10^5 x 20 x 10^-6), the gradient of 1/V against P equals 1/(PV) = 0.494 J^-1, and the intercept must be zero, a non-zero intercept signalling a systematic error such as omitting atmospheric pressure from P

Conditions, precautions and sources of error: the law holds only for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, so the gas must be allowed to return to room temperature after each compression (compression warms it and makes PV drift upward) and the closed limb must be gas-tight; other precautions are keeping the tube vertical, taking h as the difference of the two mercury levels, and avoiding parallax at the convex meniscus, while further error sources are dead space or a non-uniform bore, moisture in the trapped air adding a saturated vapour pressure, uncertainty in rho, g and the barometric reading, and real-gas deviation at high pressure

courses.name: Nigerian Peoples and Culture
weekTopics: Citizenship is described as the state of being a citizen, as well as the rights, obligations and advantages that come with it: with citizenship of a nation you have the right to live, work, vote and pay taxes there, it is usually granted in the nation where you were born, and an immigrant from another nation must apply; the lesson warns that citizenship is often confused with nationality, which is of a wider scope than citizenship

The Nigerian Constitution from the time of independence provides for some types of citizenship, but before the date of independence there were no Nigerian citizens, and since 1979 there have been significant changes in the law relating to citizenship, the instruments named being the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1979, the Nigeria Citizenship Act 1960 and the Nigerian Citizenship Act 1961; every country has the right to decide who will be its citizen, and Chapter Three of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended) provides extensively for citizenship in Nigeria through exactly three routes - by birth, by registration and by naturalisation

Citizenship by birth under the 1999 Constitution arises where both parents are Nigerians, or either parent is a Nigerian, or any one of the grandparents is a Nigerian - the three limbs are alternatives, so a single qualifying relative suffices and no requirement of birth on Nigerian soil is imposed

Citizenship by registration is open to two classes only: a non-Nigerian woman who is married to a Nigerian, and every person of full age and capacity born outside Nigeria whose grandparent is a citizen of Nigeria; to qualify, the foreigner must prove to the President that he or she is a person of good character, has shown a clear intention of the desire to be domiciled or to live or reside in Nigeria, and has taken the prescribed Oath of Allegiance to Nigeria contained in the Seventh Schedule to the 1999 Constitution

Naturalisation is the process by which an individual becomes a legal citizen of a specific country, the formal act of granting citizenship to a foreign national who meets the predetermined eligibility criteria established by that country's laws and regulations; in Nigeria it is done by fulfilling the requirements stipulated in section 27 of the 1999 Constitution, after which a certificate of grant of citizenship by naturalisation is issued, and it is the means by which any foreigner who has lived for a long time in Nigeria may become a Nigerian citizen

Dual citizenship is allowed: a foreigner who is a citizen of another country by birth may also be a citizen of Nigeria by registration or by naturalisation, and a Nigerian citizen by birth may acquire the citizenship of another country without renouncing his Nigerian citizenship; a citizen of full age may renounce and abandon Nigerian citizenship by the prescribed declaration, but the President may refuse to register that declaration where it is made when Nigeria is involved in a war or where it is contrary to public policy

Loss of citizenship reaches only acquired citizenship: the President may deprive a person who is not a Nigerian by birth where that person is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 3 years within a period of 7 years after becoming a citizen by naturalisation, and persons who acquired citizenship by naturalisation or by registration may lose it for disloyalty to Nigeria by act or speech, for trading with or associating in business with an enemy country at war with Nigeria, for assisting such an enemy country in any manner, or for unlawfully communicating with it to the detriment of or with intent to damage Nigeria

Civic responsibility is the duties and obligations that citizens are expected to fulfil for the betterment of their society and the functioning of their country, outlined in various laws, policies and cultural expectations; the six named are obeying the law, protection of public property, payment of taxes, rendering national service, loyalty and respect for others' rights, and they are contained in section 24 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended), which makes it the duty of every citizen to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, the National Anthem, the National Pledge and legitimate authorities; to help enhance the power, prestige and good name of Nigeria, defend Nigeria and render such national service as may be required; to respect the dignity of other citizens and the rights and legitimate interests of others and live in unity and harmony in the spirit of common brotherhood; to make positive and useful contribution to the advancement, progress and well-being of the community where he resides; to render assistance to appropriate and lawful agencies in the maintenance of law and order; and to declare his income honestly to appropriate and lawful agencies and pay his tax promptly - civic responsibility being not only a legal obligation but also a moral duty that promotes active citizenship and contributes to the overall development of Nigeria

courses.name: Communication in English II
weekTopics: Vocabulary expansion defined as the process of increasing one's repertoire of words and expressions in a language, a fundamental aspect of language development that supports effective communication, cognitive growth, academic success and overall linguistic proficiency

The seven word formation processes the lesson names - affixation, compounding, conversion, derivation, blending, acronyms and borrowing - each with the deck's own example: unadulterated and correctly, raincoat, email used as a verb, teacher, brunch, NASA and sushi

Affixes as bound forms attached to an existing base: prefixes go before the base (un- in unadulterated, meaning 'not') and suffixes after it (-ly in correctly), and their stated function is to alter meaning and function while expanding vocabulary

The distinctions that carry the marks: compounding merges two whole words while blending fuses only parts of them, conversion changes word class with no affix at all while derivation adds a derivational affix to create a new word, and an acronym is pronounced as a word (NASA) while an initialism is spelled out (ATM)

Derivational versus inflectional affixes: a derivational suffix makes a new lexeme with its own dictionary entry and usually a new word class (teach -> teacher, happy -> happiness), whereas inflectional -s, -ed, -ing, -er and -est only mark number, tense or degree and create no new word

Suffixes grouped by the word class they produce - nouns from -tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -er, -ist and -ship; adjectives from -ful, -less, -able, -ive, -ous, -al and -ic; verbs from -ise, -ify, -en and -ate; adverbs from -ly - and prefixes grouped by meaning, including negation (un-, in-, non-, dis-), repetition (re-), error (mis-), time (pre-, post-) and number (mono-, bi-, multi-)

The seven benefit headings for vocabulary expansion - communication skills, intellectual growth, academic achievement, professional success, cultural competence, lifelong learning, and reading and writing proficiency - together with the four named strategies: reading widely and regularly, using vocabulary-building tools such as dictionaries, thesauruses and language-learning apps, engaging in conversations, discussions and debates, and playing word games and language-related activities

The academic word list to be known by definition rather than recognition, including pedagogy, epistemology, didactic and didacticism, elocution, lexicon, dissertation, thesis, cacophony, syllogism, semiotics, metacognition, exegesis, synthesis, mentorship, scholarship, curriculum, citation, prerequisite, peer review, academic rigor, academician, seminar, tenure, quantitative analysis, rubric and interdisciplinary, plus the Technolingo case study on how tech neologisms are coined and analysed etymologically

courses.name: Introduction to Web Technologies
weekTopics: The distinction between a library and a framework turns on control flow: a library is pre-written code that your program calls while you keep control, whereas a framework provides the whole application's structure and calls your code at the points it defines

JavaScript libraries are pre-written collections of functions integrated into a project to simplify development; jQuery's five named features are DOM manipulation, event handling, AJAX requests, animation and cross-browser compatibility

Lodash is a utility library for arrays, objects and strings that emphasises method chaining, functional programming and efficient processing of large datasets, while Moment.js handles date parsing, formatting, date arithmetic, timezones and locales

Choosing a library depends on project requirements, library size and page-load impact, whether modern native JavaScript already covers the need, team familiarity, and the library's maintenance and longevity

React is a component-based UI library from Facebook that uses a virtual DOM (it tracks the difference between the virtual DOM and the actual DOM and updates only the parts that differ) and enforces unidirectional data flow from parent to child

Angular is Google's comprehensive framework built on modules and components, with dependency injection managing the creation and sharing of services and two-way data binding synchronising UI and model in both directions, while Vue.js is a progressive, incrementally adoptable view-layer framework using directives and components with a gentle learning curve; the choice between them turns on requirements, team familiarity, community, scalability and learning curve

Backend frameworks studied: Django (Python, MVC, generated admin interface, built-in authentication and authorization, DRY), Express.js (Node.js, minimalist and flexible, routing and template engines), Ruby on Rails (Convention over Configuration, DRY, Active Record ORM, RESTful routing, scaffolding) and ASP.NET (C#, MVC and Razor Pages, cross-platform ASP.NET Core, Visual Studio tooling)

Express.js middleware functions have access to the request and response objects in the request-response cycle and execute in the order they are defined, forming a custom pipeline for authentication, logging and data parsing before the route handler runs

Conceptual session on Week 8 integration techniques, exactly as she builds them.

The standard-integral table of slides 4–6.

Her substitution formula ∫f′(g(x))·g′(x)dx = f(g(x)) + C, and when an answer may be left in u.

Integration by parts ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du, and why v is the integral of dv.
